summary: Part 2 of the 11.0 Dashboard (KAMs) video (06:52-13:45) is a tour of the Supply dashboard. In the Daily tab the trainer walks the morning checks (late and stuck orders, unidentified carriers, refund policy clock, claims coverage), then the KAM tab (HR performance and bonus scoring, career, sellers charts, semi-active list). All 40 frames in the pack were opened and checked. Numbers are snapshot values from the recording (refund policy snapshot 2026-10-16). Several spoken numbers were corrected or confirmed from on-screen text, and some points are unclear or unverifiable on screen.

terms.meaning: Orders shown in the Daily Late orders list, sorted oldest first with days since order and stage. The exact definition of late is not given in the video (Methodology not opened).
Orders that shipped at least four days ago and still have no delivered date.
Orders are delivered but not marked delivered, because in markets with no courier delivery feed nobody has marked them.
Shipped orders whose tracking record names no shipping company (a missing record).
The delivery time promised for a market, shown in the SLA column; the narration and caption state three working days in the Emirates and five elsewhere.
The clock counts working hours the claim spends in stages the seller owns. A policy day is 24 weekday hours on the Dubai calendar day; Saturday and Sunday never accrue.
Returns whose clock is running because the claim sits with the seller (dark blue on the chart).
Returns whose clock is frozen because the claim is on Revibe's side (light blue on the chart; banked, frozen until it restarts).
Policy days that carry a warning marker on the market axis: 7 and 8 for Saudi Arabia; 6 and 7 for the other markets.
Policy days that carry the red policy-applied marker: 9 and above for Saudi Arabia; 8 and above for the other markets. A claim in those columns is one Revibe can act on.
Per month, claims raised split into closed (green) and still open (red); the closed share is the coverage, and higher is better.
Switches Claims coverage bars between counts (Volume) and shares (%, every bar full height).
Metric read one period back, used for the defect rate because claims arrive weeks after the order.
A month runs from the 20th of the previous month to the 19th of the month, for example October is 20 Sep to 19 Oct.
The score of each KPI for the current period, from 0 at Min to 100% at Base and 150% at High.
The weighted sum of KPI scores, capped at 150%.
The three thresholds for each KPI on the scoring scale.
Monthly variable salary.
Total multiplied by the bonus baseline.
Adjustment column and send-to-payroll button; greyed out for the KAM and used by Pierre to set the final figure.
Sellers with between 1 and 29 orders so far this month.
A seller with at least one order.
A seller with 30 or more orders in the month.
New seller is a seller on its first order; new active seller is one with 30 or more direct orders in its first month (per the legend).
A seller flagged as closed buybox; the video says to reopen closed buyboxes each morning. The exact meaning is not defined in the video.
